Schema: The Prisma schema file (schema.prisma) defines data sources, generators, and models. It serves as the single source of truth for your database schema with a declarative DSL.

datasource db { provider = 'postgresql' url = env('DATABASE_URL') } generator client { provider = 'prisma-client-js' } model User { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) email String @unique name String? posts Post[] createdAt DateTime @default(now()) }
Migrations: Prisma Migrate generates SQL migration files from schema changes and applies them to the database. Migrations track history and support rollbacks.
npx prisma migrate dev --name init && npx prisma migrate dev --name add_profile && npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma migrate status
Prisma Client: Prisma Client is an auto-generated, type-safe database client. It provides a fluent API for CRUD, filtering, pagination, relations, and transactions.

import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'; const prisma = new PrismaClient(); async function main() { const users = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { role: 'ADMIN' }, include: { posts: true } }); console.log(users); } main().finally(() => prisma.$disconnect());

Models: Models represent database tables with strongly-typed fields. Each field has attributes like @id, @unique, @default, and relation attributes. Native database types map to Prisma types.

model Product { id String @id @default(cuid()) name String slug String @unique description String? price Decimal @db.Decimal(10,2) inventory Int @default(0) categoryId Int category Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id]) reviews Review[] @@index([categoryId]) }
Relations: Relations define connections between models using @relation and foreign keys. Supports one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many with both required and optional sides.

model User { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) posts Post[] profile Profile? } model Post { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) userId Int user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id]) }
Attributes: Attributes decorate fields with ID, default, uniqueness, constraint, and indexing metadata. Key attributes: @id, @default, @unique, @updatedAt, @map, @db.*, @@unique, @@index.
model User { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) email String @unique cognitoId String @unique @map('cognito_id') role Role @default(USER) @@map('users') @@index([role]) } enum Role { USER ADMIN }

Create: Prisma Client provides create, createMany, and upsert for inserting data. Nested writes create related records simultaneously in a single transaction.
const user = await prisma.user.create({ data: { email: 'alice@test.com', name: 'Alice', posts: { create: { title: 'First post' } } }, include: { posts: true } });
Read: Read operations include findUnique, findFirst, findMany, and count. They support filtering, sorting, pagination, relation inclusion, and field selection.

const users = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { name: { contains: 'alice' } }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, take: 10, skip: 0, include: { posts: true } }); const total = await prisma.user.count();
Update: Update operations include update, updateMany, and upsert. Update modifies existing records matching the where condition with the provided data.
const updated = await prisma.user.update({ where: { email: 'alice@test.com' }, data: { name: 'Alice Updated', role: 'ADMIN' } });
Delete: Delete operations include delete and deleteMany. Delete removes a single record by unique identifier, while deleteMany removes all matching records.
await prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: 1 } }); await prisma.user.deleteMany({ where: { isActive: false } });

Nested Writes: Nested writes create, update, or delete related records within a single operation. Prisma handles the transaction automatically across all related models.

const user = await prisma.user.create({ data: { email: 'bob@test.com', posts: { create: [{ title: 'Post 1' }, { title: 'Post 2' }] }, profile: { create: { bio: 'Hello' } } }, include: { posts: true, profile: true } });
Filtering Relations: Filter queries by relation conditions using some, every, none, and is. This enables complex queries like finding users with at least one published post.
const users = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { posts: { some: { published: true } } }, include: { posts: { where: { published: true } } } });
Pagination: Prisma supports offset pagination (skip/take) and cursor-based pagination (cursor/skip/take) for efficient navigation through large datasets.
const page = await prisma.user.findMany({ take: 10, skip: 20, orderBy: { id: 'asc' } }); const cursor = await prisma.user.findMany({ take: 10, cursor: { id: 50 }, skip: 1, orderBy: { id: 'asc' } });

Group By: Prisma groupBy enables aggregation queries with grouping, counting, summing, averaging, min, and max operations across specified fields.
const stats = await prisma.user.groupBy({ by: ['role'], _count: { id: true }, _avg: { age: true }, _sum: { points: true } });
Aggregates: Aggregate functions compute count, sum, avg, min, and max values across all matching records. Useful for dashboards and reporting.
const result = await prisma.order.aggregate({ _count: { id: true }, _sum: { amount: true }, _avg: { amount: true }, _max: { amount: true } });
Raw Queries: Raw queries execute custom SQL for operations not supported by Prisma's query API. Use $queryRaw for SELECT and $executeRaw for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

const users = await prisma.$queryRaw('SELECT id, email, name FROM users WHERE role = $1', 'ADMIN'); const result = await prisma.$executeRaw('UPDATE users SET points = points + 10 WHERE is_active = true');

Create & Deploy: Migration workflows: migrate dev for development (auto-generates and applies), migrate deploy for production (applies pending migrations), and migrate reset for testing.
npx prisma migrate dev --name add_user_table && npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma migrate reset --force
Seed: Database seeding populates tables with initial or test data. Prisma seeding uses a seed script configured in package.json and runs with prisma db seed.

// prisma/seed.js: const { PrismaClient } = require('@prisma/client'); const prisma = new PrismaClient(); async function main() { await prisma.user.createMany({ data: [{ email: 'admin@test.com', role: 'ADMIN' }, { email: 'user@test.com' }] }); } main().finally(() => prisma.$disconnect()); // package.json: { 'prisma': { 'seed': 'node prisma/seed.js' } }
Rollback: Prisma does not support automatic rollback, but you can revert by creating a new migration that reverses the previous changes, or by restoring the database from backup.
npx prisma migrate dev --name revert_previous # Create inverse migration and npx prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 'migration_name' # Mark as rolled back

Middleware: Prisma middleware (deprecated in favor of extensions) allows intercepting queries for logging, caching, access control, and input/output transformation.

prisma.$use(async (params, next) => { console.log('Query:', params.model, params.action); const start = Date.now(); const result = await next(params); console.log('Duration:', Date.now() - start, 'ms'); return result; });
Extensions: Prisma Extensions (preview) enable model-scoped and client-scoped functionality including computed fields, access policies, and custom queries.

const prisma = new PrismaClient().$extends({ result: { user: { fullName: { needs: { firstName: true, lastName: true }, compute(user) { return user.firstName + ' ' + user.lastName; } } } }, query: { user: { async $allOperations({ args, query }) { console.log('User query'); return query(args); } } } });
Logging: Prisma Client provides configurable logging for queries, info, warnings, and errors. Useful for debugging and performance monitoring in development.

const prisma = new PrismaClient({ log: ['query', 'info', 'warn', 'error'] }); const prisma = new PrismaClient({ log: [{ emit: 'event', level: 'query' }] }); prisma.$on('query', (e) => console.log('Query:', e.query, 'Params:', e.params, 'Duration:', e.duration, 'ms'));

Connection Pooling: Connection pooling via PgBouncer or Prisma Accelerate manages database connections efficiently, preventing connection exhaustion under load.
datasource db { provider = 'postgresql' url = env('DATABASE_URL') connection_limit = 20 } const prisma = new PrismaClient({ datasources: { db: { url: process.env.DATABASE_URL } } });
Edge: Prisma Edge Client is optimized for serverless environments like Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge. Uses HTTP-based Data Proxy instead of direct connections.

import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client/edge'; const prisma = new PrismaClient({ datasourceUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL }); export default async function handler(req) { const users = await prisma.user.findMany(); return new Response(JSON.stringify(users)); }
Production: Production considerations: connection pooling, migration safety, timeouts, error-only logging, environment variables, and graceful shutdown.

const prisma = new PrismaClient(); async function safeQuery(fn) { try { return await fn(); } catch (error) { if (error.code === 'P2002') throw new Error('Duplicate'); if (error.code === 'P2025') throw new Error('Not found'); throw error; } } process.on('SIGTERM', async () => { await prisma.$disconnect(); process.exit(0); });

Accelerate Overview: Prisma Accelerate is a global cache and connection pooler that sits between your app and database. It caches queries at the edge, reduces connection overhead, and provides real-time analytics.
Caching Strategies: Accelerate supports TTL-based caching with swr and ttl options per query. Cached responses serve instantly from the edge while the database is updated asynchronously.
Connection Pooling: Accelerate replaces direct database connections with HTTP-based queries through a global connection pool, eliminating connection limits in serverless environments and cold starts.

Real-time Changes: Prisma Pulse provides real-time database change streaming. It emits events when rows are created, updated, or deleted, enabling reactive UIs without polling or WebSocket boilerplate.
Pulse with Accelerate: Pulse works with Accelerate to stream changes through the edge network. Combined, they provide cached reads and real-time write propagation for globally distributed applications.

MongoDB Provider: Prisma supports MongoDB as a data source provider with schemas, relations, and embedded documents. MongoDB models use @map and @db attributes for BSON type mapping.
Embedded Documents: MongoDB embedded documents are represented as JSON fields with @db.ObjectId for referencing. Prisma supports ObjectId, String, Int, Float, and Boolean BSON types for MongoDB fields.

model Profile {
  id     String @id @default(auto()) @map('_id') @db.ObjectId
  bio    String
  stats  Json   // Embedded document as JSON
  userId String @unique @db.ObjectId
  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
}
MongoDB Relations: MongoDB relations use ObjectId references with the same relation syntax as SQL databases. However, compound unique constraints are not supported, and referential actions are implemented at the application level.

model Post {
  id      String @id @default(auto()) @map('_id') @db.ObjectId
  title   String
  content String?
  authorId String @db.ObjectId
  author   User  @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
}

onDelete: Referential actions control what happens to related records when a parent record is deleted. Prisma supports Cascade, Restrict, NoAction, SetNull, and SetDefault for foreign key constraints.
onUpdate: onUpdate referential action specifies behavior when a parent's referenced field changes. These actions map to database-level ON UPDATE constraints and are validated during migrations.
Referential Action Types: Cascade propagates delete/update to related records. Restrict prevents delete if relations exist. NoAction defers to the database. SetNull sets foreign keys to NULL. SetDefault uses the default value.
